findings: Medium (scope of `fault`). `fault` is narrower than memory- and type-safety: Store.write/modify accept a value of any shape or type at an existing location (the model has no type check on write, no mutability tag on Val.ref, and no const check). With --no-validate, a module that stores a bool in an i64 variable and prints it runs to `done` printing `true`, not a fault (w1 in the reviewer's runs). The theorem excludes such programs only because validate rejects them; the typed-store facts live in the proved invariant (StoreInv/Frame, validated_steps_keep_invariant), not in the headline. Anyone citing 'never faults' as 'never reads or writes at a wrong type' should cite the invariant theorems; and V-MUT (writes only through mutable places) has no theorem at all.

Medium (documentation overclaim). Spec 16.6 says the Lean safety theorem 'shows sound for the profiles'; the Lean model is core-pilot only: there is no core-shrink or core-construction syntax, no shrink rule (V-SHRINK, V-WHOLE), no nonlocal return, no limited array; spec 4.6 still lists V-SHRINK and V-WHOLE as rules of validate. The headline is for the grow-only pilot, where growth cannot invalidate anything, which is the easy half of the language's reference-safety story.

Medium (validate rejects ordinary programs that the exporter emits). Over the 2,472 .goose files in test/ and samples/, the exporter accepts 82 (the rest are unsupported or deliberate error tests); validate accepts 78 of them. The four rejections are: (a) test/optimizer/loop_shapes_countdown_abort.goose: V-MUT, the exporter emits e_slice mut over a `let` array passed to a slice parameter; (b) test/runtime/never_returns_exit.goose: V-TYPE 'falls off its end', Typing.lean's diverges does not know a call to a function that always exits; (c) test/typing/return_const_recursion.goose: V-TYPE, `let c: const T& = r` with r : T& (mut-to-const reference initialization and return are typed as an exact-equality check, while call arguments use passableTo); (d) test/runtime/elementwise_scalar_zero.goose: an exporter defect (12 / values with an array operand is exported instead of reported unsupported), which validate correctly rejects. All are rejections, never acceptances, so the theorem is unaffected, but acceptance by validate is narrower than acceptance by the compiler.
